observations: A rounded, hunched figure sits center-frame, its body built from overlapping olive, yellow, and teal scribbled lines that leave the form semi-transparent rather than solid.
Two large orange-red goggle-like circles dominate the upper face, glowing against a pale yellow haze that fans outward toward the lower right.
A smaller open-mouthed form appears at lower left, rendered in darker browns and reds, partially merged with the main figure through shared overlapping lines.
reading: The main figure sits heavily, its body assembled from restless layered lines that never fully close into solid mass. The orange goggle shapes read as eyes but glow more like lenses, giving the face a sealed, inward quality. A pale yellow wedge fans outward from the chest area, suggesting emission rather than reflected light. The smaller open-mouthed form at lower left adds unease without resolving into a clear relationship with the larger figure.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, title neighbors are nnxyz nnotb #98 and nnxyz nnotb #100. Where #98 uses a flat teal field and a single opaque black silhouette, #99 layers translucent marks to build volume, and #100 works in near-total darkness with glowing eyes.

connections.reason: Both works place a seated animal-like figure against a dark or neutral ground and use warm glowing eye shapes as the face's focal point; #100 strips away the layered line texture that gives #99 its hazy, semi-transparent volume.

Title neighbor #98 offers a direct contrast: its figure is a flat opaque black silhouette on a solid teal field, while #99 builds a similar seated posture from semi-transparent overlapping marks — two opposite approaches to the same basic shape.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly does the pale yellow wedge begin — does it originate from the figure's chest, its eyes, or somewhere else in the image?
ambiguities: The smaller open-mouthed form at lower left may be a separate figure or a fragment of the same body; the overlapping lines do not resolve this clearly.
Faint lettering appears in the upper right of the image; it is treated as artwork content, not metadata, and its meaning is not interpreted.
